public_rationale: He said OpenAI 'cannot afford to pay for the compute' in Oracle's data centers. The roughly $300B Oracle contract mostly starts in 2027, so most of the bill was not yet due at the post date or by the evaluation date. Around the post, OpenAI had about $110B in committed funding, later $122B, and was reporting about $2B a month in revenue. That cuts against near-term inability to pay. Against that, OpenAI was still unprofitable and burning cash. FT-reported projections said it could exhaust that funding by 2028 and would face large negative free cash flow through 2030. No missed or renegotiated payment to Oracle was found. The evidence cannot yet show whether OpenAI can or cannot pay, so the claim is unresolved.
limitations: Affordability depends on future revenue and financing, which an observation at the post date cannot settle.
The sources are news reports of private-company figures.

The Oracle contract (about $300B over five years) mostly begins in 2027. So affordability is largely about future payments, which an observation as of March 2026 cannot settle.
Period: the state at the post date. I use early 2026 up to 2026-03-17, the latest financial picture before the post. This choice is flagged.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that OpenAI missed, deferred or renegotiated payments due to Oracle for lack of funds, or could not raise the money needed for payments then due.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that OpenAI was paying what was due to Oracle and had cash and committed funding enough to cover the payments falling due.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has signed a contract with Oracle to buy $300 billion worth of computing power over the next five years, according to the Wall Street Journal.
evidence.explanation: The same article says the contract begins in 2027, so most payments fall due after the post. Whether OpenAI can afford them is largely a future question.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI announced that it had closed its latest funding round with $122 billion in committed capital, valuing the ChatGPT maker at $852 billion post-money. The figure is up from the $110 billion the company announced in February
evidence.explanation: Around the post date OpenAI had about $110B (later $122B) in committed funding. That counts against near-term inability to pay, though the same article says it was still burning cash and unprofitable.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI raised $122bn in March at an $852bn valuation, and the FT reports it is on track to exhaust that by 2028. The projection period runs two years beyond the money.
evidence.locator: section 'The clock is the other story'
evidence.explanation: Projections show OpenAI would need more financing before 2028 to cover its compute plans. This supports his concern about future affordability, but it is a projection, not a missed payment.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Disclosure of OpenAI's payments to Oracle once the contract ramps in 2027, such as missed, deferred or renegotiated payments, or Oracle reporting OpenAI paying in full. An OpenAI IPO prospectus showing cash against contracted obligations would also help.
